transcript.fullText: At the age of 16, I was adopted by a regular family. My younger sister, Regina Capasso, was taken in by a mafia don, resulting in her becoming the principessa of Italia's most powerful mafia family. Unexpectedly, Regina was cast out by the don in her first month of getting adopted. I, on the other hand, got into a prestigious university thanks to my good grades. I rose to fame in the AI industry, married my adopted brother Dario Digona, and lived a happy life. Yet, on the very day of the wedding, Regina rushed [music] out from the crowd, grabbed a knife, stabbed it through my heart. When I opened my eyes again, I had been reborn to the day we were adopted. Regina made a decision completely different from her previous life. She rushed into Dario's arms while gazing at me gloatingly. "You should have a taste of what it feels like to be a principessa, Livia." It turned out that she was also reborn. I looked at Dario, my husband in my last life, expecting him to say something, but instead, he shielded Regina like a prized possession. >> Stay away from my sister. >> His cold gaze turned to me. Dario had no memories of his last life. To him, I was just a stranger. Just then, the Rolls-Royce sent by the mafia family stopped in front of me. The butler opened the rear door and invited me to get in. >> Signorina, please get in the car. >> In our last life, when we had to choose, Regina had eagerly hopped into the Rolls-Royce. She had turned around and said to me smiling, "Livia, I'll be the principessa. You go live that poor life. I'm still too young for that kind of life. You'll suffer for me, right?" But this time, she linked arms with Dario and watched smugly as I got into this Rolls-Royce. "I hope you can live a little longer in that cool family." The car slowly started moving. The butler, sitting in the front seat, silently observed me through the rearview mirror. About 10 minutes into the drive, he passed me a file. >> I'm the Vigione family's butler. Here are some things to keep in mind when you get to Vigione estate. The mafia is all about rules, so be careful not to step out of line. >> I'll keep that in mind. The car soon arrived at Vicino estate. I followed the butler into the luxurious mansion, which looked like a palace. Not far away, a tall man stood by the floor-to-ceiling window, his back to us. The butler stepped forward and bowed respectfully. >> Don Vicino, she's here. >> The tall man turned around, a cup of coffee in his hand. His gaze swept over me, taking me in. His deep voice rang out as he sat down on the couch, waving me over. >> Come here. What's your name? >> Livia. >> No need to change your name. Just take the Vicino surname. I'm your papa, Alano Vicino. From now on, this is your home. >> He gestured to the beautiful woman by his side. >> This is your mama, Immalida Totini. If you need anything, just tell her. Don't be shy. >> Thank you, papa, mama. The butler took me to my room. As I stepped inside, I was instantly enveloped in a cocoon of warm pink. Everything in the room was on a level that most people could only dream of, and yet here I was, obtaining it all so effortlessly from my adoptive parents. I was smiling, daydreaming about the bright future ahead, when suddenly the door was kicked open with a loud bang. My brain froze as I turned around and saw a massive mastino charging toward me. Just as the mastino knocked me to the ground, I noticed a young man leaning lazily against the doorframe. He was part of Vicino, Alano's only son, looking at me with disdain. The mastino he brought was known for its ferocity. In the mafia world, it was often raised as a fighting dog. But now, I was sitting up, holding the Mestino in my lap. Pardo's expression shifted. I smiled lightly. >> Why didn't Shado attack you? >> In my last life, to ensure my safety, I'd lived and slept with a Mestino for years. I knew how to handle it better than Dario. I took some jerky out of my pocket and fed it to the dog, which then sat quietly focused [snorts] on chewing its treat. And then, I looked up at Pardo. Nice to meet you, Pardo. I'm Livia. Pardo's initial disdain turned into curiosity. After a while, he scoffed. >> Shado, let's go. >> The next few days were hectic. I woke up every morning to run drills. The driver took me to the shooting range and boxing ring. Even after returning home, there were tutors to teach me about the family history and how to become a mafia princess who is useful to the family. A month later, Imelda gave me a satisfied smile. You did great. Pardo has been thoroughly spoiled by his papa and me. He's quite naive, so I'll need you to guide him whenever necessary. >> Without a moment of hesitation, I immediately responded. >> Once he becomes the Don, you'll be the underboss. What do you think? >> Sure, Mama. >> Obviously, I had gained Imelda's approval. Imelda handed me a card, gave me a day off, and had the driver take me to the city sector to buy something I liked. As soon as I stepped out of the car, I spotted a familiar face, Regina. She was wearing a red and white mascot costume holding the oversized mascot head with one hand while using a flyer to wipe the sweat off her forehead with the other. Her pale face had turned bright red from the heat, yet her face was filled with happiness and pride. On this day in her previous life, she had been thrown out of the Vicino family and had since lived a vagrant, miserable life. She naturally assumed that I was the one suffering these torments. A young man was rushing toward her. It was Dario. He too was holding a thick stack of flyers. He hurried over to Regina and used the flyers to fan her. >> Regina, are you okay? If you're tired, we can go home. >> Hearing the concern in his voice, Regina weakly smiled. >> I'm fine, Dario. But my poor sister isn't that lucky. Right now, she's probably been kicked out of the Vicino family, turned into a homeless beggar, wearing ragged clothes, and can't even afford a single meal. That's so poor. >> Just as Regina was sneering and mocking, she saw me dressed in an elegant gown and carrying a Hermes handbag. >> Who was it you said was going to be a beggar, huh? >> Regina's face froze. >> Loria? You haven't been kicked out? No freaking way! >> What did you do to my sister? >> bitten by Pardo's dog, but I came out without a scratch. In her past life, she had been kicked out of the family long ago. Well, I somehow thrived in that cutthroat, bloodsucking mafia family. Regina stared at my beautiful dress and my Hermes bag in disbelief. Jealousy and madness were written all over her face. >> do anything because she got a little taste of the good life. >> Dario, she didn't do anything because she got a little taste of the good life. >> She actually survived in a mafia family? But who's to say she won't do it >> Ignoring him, I bypassed them and walked into the mall. >> about her. >> Behind me, I heard Regina's voice dripping with fake concern. >> Regina, you're a sweet girl. Whatever happens, I've got your back. >> As soon as I stepped into the mall, their voices disappeared entirely. I used Imelda's bank card to purchase many luxury goods. As soon as I returned to the living room, I heard a [clears throat] sharp voice cutting through the air. >> You really went all out, huh? Do you really think you're the principessa of the Vicino family now? >> I ignored his mocking tone and sweetly greeted him. Pardo, I got you a gift. With that, I took the box and placed it on the coffee table in front of Pardo. Go ahead, open it. See if you like it. He sneered as he opened the box. >> You're from the slums. What kind of gift are you going to pick out? Don't tell me you brought back some junk. >> Young Master Pardo has always had very high standards. Is that woman trying to suck up to him? Let's just wait and see her gift get thrown straight to the trash, my Pardo. >> The latest gaming laptop. >> When they saw how surprised and pleased Pardo looked, those maids who had been talking trash completely froze. I couldn't help but laugh to myself, guessing I picked the right gift after all. Although a laptop like this wasn't much to the Vicino family, Pardo had been denied his allowance because of his lack of ambition, and he couldn't afford the latest version himself. When he noticed my smile, his expression immediately hardened, and he tried to act indifferent as he grabbed the box. >> You really know how to win people over. >> With that, he hurried off clutching the box. At dinner, I stepped into the dining room to find both Imelda and Pardo already seated. When Imelda saw me, she waved me over. >> Laura, I'm seriously impressed. Your tutor said you already know way more than any high school curriculum. You can skip the entrance exam entirely. >> Pardo just ate without looking up, but he didn't object. I smiled. Okay, Mom. On the first day of school, Pardo and I sat in the car. He glared at me. >> Listen up. Don't tell anyone at school that you're my sister. Else. >> I nodded at Pardo. As he got out of the car, Pardo shot me another warning look before heading into the school. I just said nothing, then turned away. As I turned, I found myself face-to-face with Dario and Regina at the school gate. Regina had clearly seen how Pardo had treated me earlier, and her face was full of contempt. >> Look at that. I knew it. You'll never be one of them. I'm so worried about you. Who knows how many more days you've got left. >> I didn't even want to deal with her, but Regina just kept going on and on bragging. >> My parents treat me so well. Dario even more so. He tutors me after school and brings me all sorts of snacks. Oh, and speaking of which, Dario got first place on the entrance exam. What about you? I don't remember seeing your name on the rankings. Don't tell me you didn't even make the top 500 rankings. >> Regina had no idea that with my past life memories, all this school stuff was easy for me. She also didn't know I skipped the entrance exam entirely, since my knowledge made it totally unnecessary. I didn't bother correcting her. You're right. I really didn't make the rankings. That only made her more smug. Boo, she let out a >> fake sigh. See, I told you. A cold-blooded family like that would never let you study. They're just using you as a human shield for Pardo. >> Regina, she's your sister, but you're not the same anymore. Don't waste too much time talking to someone with bad grades >> Regina smiled, pleased. >> Fine then, sis. Good luck. >> They finally left, and I got some peace. But Regina spread rumors about me all over school. After class, I got stopped at the gate. >> Heard you bought your way into this school and you're a total slaughter. Who's backing you? If you can't tell us you're going to get it. >> As they threatened me, Pardo stood 10 m away, just watching to see how I'd deal with it. I turned to face the students blocking my way and said calmly, "Why is it that just because someone calls me a slacker, you all believe it? If I told you I was Superman's sister, would you buy that, too?" When I said the bit about being Superman's sister, Pardo froze for 2 seconds, then let out a low chuckle. The other onlookers couldn't help but burst out laughing. >> She actually said she's Superman's sister. >> Hilarious. >> [laughter] >> Meanwhile, the students who had been threatening me clearly didn't look too happy. How about we all calm down? Whether I'm qualified to be at this school or not, we'll find out when exam results come in, won't we? The students looked at each other, clearly second-guessing themselves. After all, no one had any real proof that I didn't deserve to be at this school. >> Fine, then. We'll wait and see what ranking you get on the exams. >> Just like that, I got through the whole mess caused by Regina's rumors. Pardo's eyes held a hint of appreciation that was hard to notice. He gave me a deep look, then turned and walked out of the classroom. When I got to the school gate, I ran into Regina again. "Sister, what's the point of fooling them like that? Once exam results come out, won't everyone see you're just a slacker? When the students realize you tricked them, they'll be even angry. You don't seriously think Pardo will protect you when that day comes, do you? I clearly saw how he just stood by and watched today. Stop dreaming." I gave a calm smile. "So, I'm just supposed to wait for the punishment that comes with being a liar? Is that it? Fine. I'll wait." Ignoring the look on Regina's face, I walked to the front gate. A luxury car was waiting there for me. And Pardo was already sitting inside. After I got in, Pardo gave me a half smile and spoke. >> Superman's sister, huh? Is that right? >> Pardo's tone was no longer as icy and contemptuous as before. A faint blush spread across my cheeks. Since then, our relationship had slowly softened, and we could even exchange a few words in the car now. One day, after a month had gone by, I waited in the car for an hour, but Pardo never showed up. His phone was unreachable. It suddenly hit me. In my last life, under peer pressure, he agreed to race in the mountains and ended up in a car accident that cost him both legs. Confined to a wheelchair for the rest of his life. Earlier that day, some classmates had mentioned a race. The location of the race was the mountain area where Pardo had crashed and lost his legs in my last life. No, I couldn't let him get into another accident. I started frantically banging on the seat, urging the driver to take me to the northern mountain range. By the time we arrived, the race had already started. Several sports cars zoomed past me, and I spotted Pardo's red car swerving out of control as it crashed INTO [clears throat] THE MOUNTAINSIDE. PARDO! I RUSHED OUT. Enduring the searing heat from the car fire, I dragged Pardo from the driver's seat. >> Just as I pulled him out, someone slapped me to the ground. >> You're his sister, right? Do you think he can walk out of here alive after crossing me? >> I looked up and saw the man responsible for Pardo's accident in my last life, Monsio Sessa, the future Don of the Sessa family. A massive hand gripped my hair, dragging me away from Pardo. I swung back with a slap, yelling, "The Vitichi family will never let you get away with this." I hoped to intimidate them with the family name. But, another slap sent me crashing to the ground. >> You WHO DO YOU THINK YOU'RE YELLING AT? I DO WHAT I WANT. I'M NOT AFRAID OF THE VITICHI FAMILY. >> I lay there, disoriented, when I saw a figure approaching through my blurry vision. It was Dario. I felt a flicker OF HOPE. DARIO, HELP [crying] ME. Dario turned at the sound of my voice. And for a moment, he hesitated. >> [crying and gasps] >> But then I saw Regina pulling him away, keeping him from coming over. >> Dario, let's go. These people are mafia members. We shouldn't get involved in this crap. >> Dario hesitated for a moment, then walked away with Regina. He never once glanced at me. Monsio sneered as he looked down at me. >> Stop dreaming. No one's coming to help you today. >> He took the wrench from his man and grinned maliciously as he approached me. >> I've grown up with no one ever daring to touch me. But you you're about to learn the price of crossing me. >> With that, he swung the wrench toward my head with full force. >> [laughter] >> No! As the wrench came crashing down, I squeezed my eyes shut expecting the pain to hit, but it never came. Pardo had thrown himself in front of me at the last second. A grunt echoed in the air. The wrench slammed into Pardo's back. Blood spilled from his mouth and dripped onto me. Pardo! Pardo, wake [screaming] up! I watched helplessly as Pardo fell from my arms. >> [laughter] >> Shut up! >> Monsieur grabbed my hair and dragged me up from the ground. >> Neither of you is leaving today. >> I tugged desperately at his hand and said, "He's the Vitruchio family's only heir. If you kill him, the Vitruchio family will never forgive you. I've already contacted the butler." If you leave now, you can still make it. As soon as I said that, his grip tightened around my neck cutting off my breath. I couldn't speak. I could only watch as his cruel face leaned closer to mine. >> Who are you fooling? Today, you're going to know the price of crossing me. >> Monsieur tossed me aside then motioned to his men. They surrounded Pardo and kicked him mercilessly. Blood poured onto the ground in bright, shocking splashes. My hands shook uncontrollably and I tried to push myself up. Desperate to stop them. In my panic, my hand brushed against something. It was a gun. I raised the gun and aimed it at the men. >> Let go of my brother. >> Seeing the gun, they slowly backed off. Once they scattered, I rushed forward to pick Pardo up. >> Pardo, are you okay? I'm getting you out of here. >> I managed to hoist Pardo onto my back. Despite the pain radiating through my body, I rushed down the mountain. I just needed to get to the bottom of the mountain, we'd be safe. But just when I was a step away from the bottom, I felt a tug from behind me. Someone grabbed Pardo and dragged him back to the ground. His wounds were aggravated and he coughed up blood. Barely able to breathe, I turned to see Mansio's cruel smile. >> You really think you can leave? >> His men closed in around us and started laughing. A massive scarred man stepped forward. Although I had trained in boxing, facing this giant was beyond my ability. >> me. Go. >> Pardo's weak voice reached me. I grabbed his arm, holding onto him tightly. >> No, I won't leave alone. We'll leave together. >> Mansio slowly clapped. >> Such touching sibling affection. >> His eyes glinted with malice as he mocked us. >> Let me make the decision for you. Neither of you is leaving. >> He waved his hand and the scarred man kicked us to the ground. The surrounding men closed in. I heard iron rods scraping against the ground and saw someone pull out a gun. I threw myself on top of Pardo, shielding him. Pardo couldn't get hurt, not now, not ever. I repeated those words in my mind, bracing for the pain. Then a loud bang rang out, and the iron rod of the person at the front fell to the ground. It was the Vicinos. They had arrived. >> Who dares to lay a hand on the Vicino family's young Don and Principessa? >> With a few gunshots, they took down all of Manchio's men. I urgently grabbed the butler to take Pardo to the hospital. >> Pardo isn't going to make IT IF WE DON'T HURRY! >> PARDO HAD ALREADY been severely injured in the car accident. If he didn't get treatment soon, his life would be at risk. I couldn't let my thoughts go any further. Unease clouded my mind. After the butler finally got Pardo into the operating room, I felt my racing heart slow down. Suddenly, everything went black, and I lost consciousness. When I woke up, a full day had passed. I opened my eyes and found Imelda sitting beside my hospital bed, holding my hand. >> Lowry, you're finally awake. Do you feel pain anywhere? >> What about Pardo? How is he? >> At the mention of Pardo, Imelda's eyes darkened with a glint of anger. >> He's in the ICU. The doctor said as long as he wakes up, he'll be fine. This isn't the end. Your papa and I will make sure the Sessa family pays for what they've done. >> Before I could respond, a doctor entered the room with the news that Pardo had regained consciousness. Imelda and I rushed out of the ward. >> Don't worry. Mr. Viccino's leg injuries were severe, but he was brought in on time. His legs have been saved. If it had been any later, the outcome could have been much worse. Now, all he needs is rest. >> Upon hearing that, I finally let out a sigh of relief. I finally changed Pardo's fate of being crippled in his past life. Three days later, Pardo was moved to a regular ward. Alano scolded him for his recklessness, but Pardo didn't seem to care. His eyes were fixed on me. >> Livia, how are you? Are you all right? >> This was the kindest tone I had ever heard him speak to me since I joined the Viccino family. It wasn't just me, Alano and Imelda were equally taken aback. With one hand, Imelda pulled me to the bedside and she stroked Pardo's face with the other. >> You can't be so reckless anymore. Once you're discharged, you need to study hard with Livia and catch up on the training you missed. After you graduate high school, you'll be ready for family duties. >> Every time they mentioned waiting until high school graduation to join the family business, Pardo would usually protest. But this time, he nodded obediently. He turned his gaze back to me. >> All right. I'll do it with Livia. >> Imelda's grip tightened on my shoulder. At that moment, I truly felt like I had a family. Alano made sure to deal with the Sessa family once and for all. He joined forces with other mafia families to take control of all Sessa family resources, avenging both Pardo and me. Pardo spent a month in the hospital, and I took a leave of absence from school to stay with him. During that time, I helped him catch up on high school courses and boxing theory. When Pardo was discharged and returned to school, it happened to coincide with the upcoming exams. After the exams, we walked out of the school gate, only to run into two people I hated, Dario and Regina. Seeing us, Regina feigned surprise and asked, "You're actually here for the exam?" "I heard you were badly injured. Are you okay?" I ignored her and pulled Pardo to walk past them. >> Liva. >> Dario called out to me. He didn't wear his usual disdainful expression. Instead, he looked somewhat guilty. >> Are you okay? >> I remembered the day he had turned away coldly. Even a stranger wouldn't have just walked off like that. My feelings for him from my previous life finally withered away. >> I'm fine. >> I replied flatly. Just as we were about to walk away, Dario stopped me again. But Pardo couldn't take it anymore and kicked him to the ground. >> Don't you dare lay a hand on my sister, unless you have a death wish. >> Dario clutched his stomach, clearly wanting to say something, but Regina stepped up to hold him back. >> Dario, let's go. Just ignore them. >> As he hesitated, Regina dragged him away. Pardo spat in their direction. >> Who do they think they are to talk to my sister? >> I couldn't help but laugh as I pulled him along. >> Enough, Pardo. Let's go home. >> Okay. I'm telling you this exam was a breeze for me. And my boxing skills have definitely improved a lot. >> I nodded seriously. I believe you. When the exam results were announced, Pardo soared into the top 10 into the top 10 at school. And I was the number one. >> Regina went wild, storming into the principal's office to demand an investigation. Even Dario couldn't stop her. She smugly warned me. >> Even if you're from the Vicino family, if they find out you cheated, you'll both be expelled. >> Dario grabbed her, his anger flaring as he demanded that she apologize to me. Regina snapped. >> Dario, YOU'RE MY BROTHER. WHY ARE YOU SIDING WITH HER? Do you have feelings for her? >> Dario didn't say anything. >> Regina, in a fit of rage, SCREAMED AT HIM. >> FINE! I [screaming] WON'T LET THEM GET AWAY WITH THIS! >> SOON AFTER, Pardo and I were summoned to the principal's office. After the school conducted its investigation, it was clear that neither Pardo nor I had cheated. On the contrary, Regina was expelled for spreading rumors and causing a scene at school. >> Why? It's them. It's their fault. WHY SHOULD I BE EXPELLED? >> Regina went wild, attempting to assault the school administrators, accusing the teacher of taking bribes from the Viceno family and targeting Dario. She demanded that the school expel the teacher. In the heat of the argument, she accidentally injured the teacher. Landing herself in a juvenile detention center. As her brother, Dario, became an outcast, subjected to bullying. Dario was so worn out from the bullying that his grades plummeted, leading to a string of warnings from his homeroom teacher. If he couldn't get his scores back up, he'd be expelled. [music] Amid the gossip, Pardo and I were in the middle of a heated debate over a math problem. I felt a burning gaze and looked up to find Dario watching us. He looked frail and haggard now. I was so focused on convincing Pardo about the problem that I didn't spare Dario another glance. As graduation day approached, both Pardo and I began taking over family affairs. We were immersing ourselves in learning to manage the family business, leaving us no time to worry about anyone else. On graduation day, everyone was celebrating. Pardo rushed home to prepare for the graduation party. As I stood by the school gate, I saw a familiar figure waiting for me. Dario? He had lost so much weight. His cheeks were sunken and his overall appearance was pitiful. He slowly walked toward me and asked, >> Which college are you going to? >> I was taken aback. What does it matter to you? >> I distinctly remembered how he had always despised me in this life. Even going as far as forbidding Regina from approaching me. After a moment of silence, he hesitated before speaking again. >> I've been having this recurring dream lately. In it, you're my sister and we even get married. We were so happy. >> He looked at me with such hopeful eyes that I was briefly dazed. He must have remembered his last life, too. But, unfortunately, I gave him a faint smile. >> You said it yourself. It's just a dream. >> Ignoring his shattered expression, I walked toward the car waiting for me. And so, I finally severed ties with my last life and stepped into a brand new future that was all mine.

transcript.fullText: On my 20th birthday, I had to choose a husband before all of Olympus. Everyone thought I would choose Apollo's Olympian, the radiant heir of the sun god, and the man I had loved for years. In my last life, I did. Because of me, he gained Zeus's favor, sacred estates, and the right to rise above every divine heir. But after our marriage, he gave his sunlight to Syltest, the dying flower nymph my mother had taken in. >> Your light was meant to belong to Persephone. >> And who else would be worthy if not you? >> When Demeter drove her away, Apollo blamed me, hated me, and finally let my sacred medicine become slow poison. >> Apollo, please, save our child. >> So, you finally figured it out? >> It was you. I loved you for 10 years. >> That was your choice. No one ever asked you to love me. Persephone, my daughter, who will you choose to be your husband? >> Faced with Zeus's question, I spoke the name without hesitation. Cassian. The last bloodline of Hades, the cursed prince of the underworld whom everyone mocked. The sons of the old houses went quiet when they saw me. >> Look who came back to beg again. Persephone really cannot stay away from Apollo's sunshine. >> A daughter of Zeus chasing a man like a lovesick mortal. Olympus must be proud. >> [laughter] >> If the old king knew she was using his oath to force a marriage, even the thunder would be ashamed. >> They didn't bother lowering their voices. In my last life, every word would would cut me. Now, I looked at Apollo and felt nothing but a clean, cold distance. He looked me over with familiar contempt. >> What are you doing in my grandfather's wing? Asking Lord Zeus to plead for you? Or reminding him that your mother's blood once saved Olympus during the Titan raids? >> Zeus summoned me. Tomorrow is my 20th birthday. He will host the choosing himself. >> [snorts] >> Everyone knew Zeus's oath. The man I chose would receive my dowry, access to the thunder vaults, and the right to stand beside me in the new council. In my last life, I had chosen Apollo and placed a crown in his hands. He stepped closer, already smiling like a victor. >> After marriage, we will live by sensible rules. I will not be tied to one woman, and you will not interfere with the healings I perform for Celeste. If you can accept that, I may treat you kindly. >> I almost laughed. He spoke as if I were still waiting for scraps. Before I could answer, a soft cough came from the far archway. Celeste crossed the hall in a pale green gown, her hair braided with white blossoms. The sound was smaller than the one he had given me, but it carried farther because everyone was waiting for it. >> You clung to me because my light kept you alive. Do not mistake pity for love. She has excellent judgment. >> Apollo had once filled rooms with speeches and left me starving. Cassian sent notes instead of excuses, and each one said where he was, when he would return, and whether I needed anything before he came back. Zeus eventually handed him the lower council and the disputed estates that no one had dared govern since Hades vanished from Olympus. King called us close. >> [sighs] >> Power attracts beggars. Feed the harmless ones, chain the dangerous ones, and never confuse family with loyalty. I will remember. >> Zeus looked at me next, and for once there was no thunder in his eyes. >> You chose better than the court deserved. >> Not long after, he died. And Olympus mourned loudly enough. Without steady solar power, her petals had begun to gray at the edges. >> No one knows where she went. A flower nimbus alone beyond temple protection is easy prey. >> I felt no triumph. Celesta had learned. She received the truth of Apollo instead. The golden heir who once believed power would always return to his hand watched it drain a coin by coin. The court was not kind to fallen sons. Men who had copied his laugh now mocked the way his light flickered at dusk. Women who had once competed for a glance from him crossed the road when he approached, afraid his bad fortune might stain their gowns. That was the first punishment Apollo truly understood. Not pain, but being ignored by the world he had taught to worship him. The next time he came to our gates, the guards didn't let him pass. His robe was stained at the hem and the light around him flickered like a lamp low on oil. >> Persephone, please. I only want to talk. That was why it killed me. >> [laughter] >> I didn't understand then. I thought you would always stay. I thought your love was part of the world, like sunrise. >> So, you stopped being grateful for it. >> I was foolish. Cruel, I know that now. Tell Cassian to help me and I will leave Olympus. I will never trouble you again. >> Do you remember the Healer's Hall? No. You wanted to talk. Do you remember hearing I was bleeding and choosing a banquet instead? Do you remember our child dying before taking one breath? >> Apollo's hands slid down the bars. >> Stop. >> No. You wanted to talk. You didn't lose me because of Celester. You didn't lose me because of Cassian. >> Persephone. >> He whispered. >> If the gods gave us another chance, why would they give it only for you to hate me? >> Maybe they gave it so I could stop hating myself. >> Behind me, Cassian crossed the courtyard. Apollo looked at him with a bitterness too tired to become rage. >> You knew she was mine once. >> Cassian's voice stayed calm. >> She was never yours. She chose you once. There is a difference. >> Apollo laughed once, broken and thin. >> So, this is my punishment? I remember everything. And she remembers everything, BUT ONLY YOU GET TO BE FORGIVEN. >> FORGIVENESS IS not a prize handed to whoever regrets the loudest. It belongs to the person who was hurt. I owe you none of it. THE HORSES ARE NOT BRIDLED! >> CRASH SPLIT THE AIR, followed by the scream of divine horses and the shattering of bronze. My steps paused, but I didn't look back. transcript.fullText: The age of 16, I was adopted by a regular family. My younger sister, Regina Capasso, was taken in by a mafia don, resulting in her becoming the principessa of Italia's most powerful mafia family. Unexpectedly, Regina was cast out by the don in her first month of getting adopted. I, on the other hand, got into a prestigious university thanks to my good grades. I rose to fame in the AI industry, married my adoptive brother, Dario Digonna, and lived a happy life. Yet, on the very day of the wedding, Regina [music] rushed out from the crowd, grabbed a knife, stabbed it through my heart. When I opened my eyes again, I had been reborn to the day we were adopted. Regina made a decision completely different from her previous life. She rushed into Dario's arms while gazing at me gloatingly. "You should have a taste of what it feels like to be a principessa, Olivia." It turned out that she was also reborn. I looked at Dario, my husband in my last life, expecting him to say something, but instead, he shielded Regina like a prized possession. >> Stay away from my sister. >> His cold gaze turned to me. Dario had no memories of his last life. To him, I was just a stranger. Just then, the Rolls-Royce sent by the mafia family stopped in front of me. The butler opened the rear door and invited me to get in. >> Signorina, please get in the car. >> In our last life, when we had to choose, Regina had eagerly hopped into the Rolls-Royce. She had turned around and said to me, smiling, >> "Olivia, I'll be the principessa. You go live that poor life. I'm still too young for that kind of life. You'll suffer for me, right?" >> But this time, she linked arms with Dario and watched smugly as I got into this Rolls-Royce. >> I hope you can live a little longer in that cruel family. >> The car slowly started moving. The butler, sitting in the front seat, silently observed me through the rearview mirror. About 10 minutes into the drive, he passed me a file. >> I'm the Vigione family's butler. Here are some things to keep in mind when you get to Vigione estate. The mafia is all about rules, so be careful not to step out of line. >> I'll keep that in mind. The car soon arrived at Vicino estate. I followed the butler into the luxurious mansion, which looked like a palace. Not far away, a tall man stood by the floor-to-ceiling window, his back to us. The butler stepped forward and bowed respectfully. >> Don Vicino, she's here. >> The tall man turned around, a cup of coffee in his hand. His gaze swept over me, taking me in. His deep voice rang out as he sat down on the couch, waving me over. >> Come here. What's your name? >> Livia. >> No need to change your name. Just take the Viccio surname. I'm your papa, Alano Vicci. From now on, this is your home. >> He gestured to the beautiful woman by his side. >> This is your mama, Immalata Totini. If you need anything, just tell her. Don't be shy. >> Thank you, papa, mama. The butler took me to my room. As I stepped inside, I was instantly enveloped in a cocoon of warm pink. Everything in the room was on a level that most people could only dream of, and yet here I was, obtaining it all so effortlessly from my adoptive parents. I was smiling, daydreaming about the bright future ahead, when suddenly the door was kicked open with a loud bang. My brain froze as I turned around and saw a massive Mastino charging toward me. Just as the Mastino knocked me to the ground, I noticed a young man leaning lazily against the doorframe. He was Parto Vicino, Alano's only son, looking at me with disdain. The Mastino he brought was known for its ferocity. In the mafia world, it was often raised as a fighting dog. But now, I was sitting up, holding the Mestino in my lap. Pardo's expression shifted. I smiled lightly. >> Why didn't Shadow attack you? >> In my last life, to ensure my safety, I'd lived and slept with a Mestino for years. I knew how to handle it better than Dario. I took some jerky out of my pocket and fed it to the dog, which then sat quietly, focused on chewing its treat. And then, I looked up at Pardo. Nice to meet you, Pardo. I'm Livia. Pardo's initial disdain turned into curiosity. After a while, he scoffed. >> Shadow, let's go. >> The next few days were hectic. I woke up every morning to run drills. The driver took me to the shooting range and boxing ring. Even after returning home, there were tutors to teach me about the family history and how to become a mafia princess who is useful to the family. A month later, Imelda gave me a satisfied smile. You did great. Pardo has been thoroughly spoiled by his papa and me. He's quite naive, so I'll need you to guide him whenever necessary. >> Without a moment of hesitation, I immediately responded. >> Once he becomes the Don, you'll be the underboss. What do you think? >> Sure, Mama. >> Obviously, I had gained Imelda's approval. Imelda handed me a card, gave me a day off, and had the driver take me to the city sector to buy something I liked. As soon as I stepped out of the car, I spotted a familiar face, Regina. She was wearing a red and white mascot costume, holding the oversized mascot head with one hand while using a flyer to wipe the sweat off her forehead with the other. Her pale face had turned bright red from the heat, yet her face was filled with happiness and pride. On this day in her previous life, she had been thrown out of the Vicino family and had since lived a vagrant, miserable life. She naturally assumed that I was the one suffering these torments. A young man was rushing toward her. It was Dario. He too was holding a thick stack of flyers. He hurried over to Regina and used the flyers to fan her. >> Regina, are you okay? If you're tired, we can go home. >> Hearing the concern in his voice, Regina weakly smiled. >> I'm fine, Dario, but my poor sister isn't that lucky. Right now, she's probably been kicked out of the Vicino family, turned into a homeless beggar wearing ragged clothes, and can't even afford a single meal. That's so poor. >> Just as Regina was sneering and mocking, she saw me dressed in an elegant gown and carrying a Hermes handbag. Who was it you said was going to be a beggar, huh? Regina's face froze. >> Loria? You haven't been kicked out? No freaking way! >> What did you do to my sister? >> bitten by Pardo's dog, but I came out without a scratch. In her past life, she had been kicked out of the family long ago. Well, I somehow thrived in that cutthroat, bloodsucking mafia family. Regina stared at my beautiful dress and my Hermes bag in disbelief. Jealousy and madness were written all over her face. >> Dario, don't be so harsh to my sister. Actually, thought I didn't do anything because she got a little taste of the good life. She actually survived in a mafia family. But who's to say she >> Ignoring him, I bypassed them and walked into the mall. >> worried about her. >> Behind me, I heard Regina's voice dripping with fake concern. >> Regina, you're a sweet girl. Whatever happens, I've got your back. >> As soon as I stepped into the mall, their voices disappeared entirely. I used Imelda's bank card to purchase many luxury goods. As soon as I returned to the living room, I heard a sharp voice cutting through the air. >> You really went all out, huh? Do you really think you're the principessa of the Vicino family now? >> I ignored his mocking tone and sweetly greeted him. Pardo, I got you a gift. With that, I took the box and placed it on the coffee table in front of Pardo. Go ahead, open it. See if you like it. He sneered as he opened the box. >> You're from the slums. What kind of gift are you going to pick out? Don't tell me you brought back some junk. >> Young Master Pardo has always had very high standards. Is that woman trying to suck up to him? >> Let's just wait and see her gift get thrown straight to the trash by Pardo. >> The latest gaming laptop. >> When they saw how surprised and pleased Pardo looked, those maids who had been talking trash completely froze. I couldn't help but laugh to myself. Guessing I picked the right gift after all. Although a laptop like this wasn't much to the Vicino family, Pardo had been denied his allowance because of his lack of ambition, and he couldn't afford the latest version himself. When he noticed my smile, his expression immediately hardened, and he tried to act indifferent as he grabbed the box. >> You really know how to win people over. >> With that, he hurried off clutching the box. At dinner, I stepped into the dining room to find both Imelda and Pardo already seated. When Imelda saw me, she waved me over. >> Laura, I'm seriously impressed. Your tutor said you already know way more than any high school curriculum. You can skip the entrance exam entirely. >> Pardo just ate without looking up, but he didn't object. >> I smiled. Okay, Mom. On the first day of school, Pardo and I sat in the car. He glared at me. >> Listen up. Don't tell anyone at school that you're my sister. Else. >> I nodded at Pardo as he got out of the car. Pardo shot me another warning look before heading into the school. I just said nothing, then turned away. As I turned, I found myself face-to-face with Dario and Regina at the school gate. Regina had clearly seen how Pardo had treated me earlier, and her face was full of contempt. >> Look at that. I knew it. You'll never be one of them. I'm so worried about you. Who knows how many more days you've got left? >> I didn't even want to deal with her, but Regina just kept going on and on bragging. >> My parents treat me so well. Dario even more so. He tutors me after school and brings me all sorts of snacks. Oh, and speaking of which, Dario got first place on the entrance exam. What about you? I don't remember seeing your name on the rankings. Don't tell me you didn't even make the top 500 rankings. >> Regina had no idea that with my past life memories, all this school stuff was easy for me. She also didn't know I skipped the entrance exam entirely since my knowledge made it totally unnecessary. I didn't bother correcting her. You're right. I really didn't make the rankings. That only made her more smug. >> Boo, she let out a fake sigh. >> See, I told you. A cold-blooded family like that would never let you study. They're just using you as a human shield for Pardo. >> Regina, she's your sister, but you're not the same anymore. Don't waste too much time talking to someone with bad grades at >> Regina smiled, pleased. Fine then, sis. Good luck. They finally left, and I got some peace. But Regina spread rumors about me all over school. After class, I got stopped at the gate. >> Heard you bought your way into this school, and you're a total slaughter. Who's backing you? If you can't tell us, you're going to get it. >> As they threatened me, Pardo stood 10 m away, just watching to see how I deal with it. I turned to face the students blocking my way, and said calmly, "Why is it that just because someone calls me a slacker, you all believe it? If I told you I was Superman's sister, would you buy that, too?" When I said the bit about being Superman's sister, Pardo froze for 2 seconds, then let out a low chuckle. The other onlookers couldn't help but burst out laughing. >> She actually said she's Superman's sister? >> It's hilarious. >> [laughter] >> Meanwhile, the students who had been threatening me clearly didn't look too happy. How about we all calm down? Whether I'm qualified to be at this school or not, we'll find out when exam results come in, won't we? The students looked at each other, clearly second-guessing themselves. After all, no one had any real proof that I didn't deserve to be at this school. >> Fine then. We'll wait and see what ranking you get on the exams. >> Just like that, I got through the whole mess caused by Regina's rumors. Pardo's eyes held a hint of appreciation that was hard to notice. He gave me a deep look, then turned and walked out of the classroom. When I got to the school gate, I ran into Regina again. Sister, what's the point of fooling them like that? Once exam results come out, won't everyone see you're just a slacker? When the students realize you tricked them, they'll be even angry. You don't seriously think Pardo will protect you when that day comes, do you? I clearly saw how he just stood by and watched today. Stop dreaming. I gave a calm smile. So, I'm just supposed to wait for the punishment that comes with being a liar? Is that it? Fine. I'll wait. Ignoring the look on Regina's face, I walked to the front gate. A luxury car was waiting there for me. And Pardo was already sitting inside. After I got in, Pardo gave me a half smile and spoke. >> Superman's sister, huh? Is that right? >> Pardo's tone was no longer as icy and contemptuous as before. A faint blush spread across my cheeks. Since then, our relationship had slowly softened, and we could even exchange a few words in the car now. One day, after a month had gone by, I waited in the car for an hour, but Pardo never showed up. His phone was unreachable. It suddenly hit me. In my last life, under peer pressure, he agreed to race in the mountains and ended up in a car accident that cost him both legs. Confined to a wheelchair for the rest of his life. Earlier that day, some classmates had mentioned a race. The location of the race was the mountain area where Pardo had crashed and lost his legs in my last life. No, I couldn't let him get into another accident. I started frantically banging on the seat, urging the driver to take me to the northern mountain range. By the time we arrived, the race had already started. Several sports cars zoomed past me, and I spotted Pardo's red car swerving out of control as it crashed INTO THE MOUNTAINSIDE. PARDO! [screaming] I RUSHED OUT. Enduring the searing heat from the car fire, I dragged Pardo from the driver's seat. Just as I pulled him out, someone slapped me to the ground. >> You're a sister, right? Do you think he can walk out of here alive after crossing me? >> I looked up and saw the man responsible for Pardo's accident in my last life, Mancio Sessa, the future Don of the Sessa family. A massive hand gripped my hair, dragging me away from Pardo. I swung back with a slap, yelling, "The Vitrucci family will never let you get away with this." I hoped to intimidate them with the family name. But, another slap sent me crashing to the ground. >> You who do you think you're yelling at? I DO WHAT I WANT. I'M NOT AFRAID OF THE VITRUCCI FAMILY. >> I lay there, disoriented, when I saw a figure approaching through my blurry vision. It was Dario. I felt a flicker of hope. DARIO, [screaming] HELP ME! Dario turned at the sound of my voice, and for a moment, he hesitated. But then I saw Regina pulling him away, keeping him from coming over. >> Dario, let's go. These people are mafia members. We shouldn't get involved in this mess. >> Dario hesitated for a moment, then walked away with Regina. He never once glanced at me. Monsio sneered as he looked down at me. >> Stop dreaming. No one's coming to help you today. >> He took the wrench from his man and grinned maliciously as he approached me. >> I've grown up with no one ever daring to touch me. But you you're about to learn the price of crossing me. >> With that, he swung the wrench toward my head with full force. >> No! >> As the wrench came crashing down, I squeezed my eyes shut, expecting the pain to hit, but it never came. Pardo had thrown himself in front of me at the last second. A grunt echoed in the air. The wrench slammed into Pardo's back. Blood spilled from his mouth and dripped onto me. I rushed to hold him, panic flooding my chest. >> Pardo! Pardo, wake up! >> I watched helplessly as Pardo fell from my arms. My hands trembled. Unable to lift him again, I kneeled beside him. >> Pardo, don't scare me. Wake up, please. >> SHUT UP! >> Monsio grabbed my hair and dragged me up from the ground. >> Neither of you is leaving today. >> I tugged desperately at his hand and said, "He's the Betucci family's only heir. If you kill him, the Betucci family will never forgive you. I've already contacted the butler. If you leave now, you can still make it." As soon as I said that, his grip tightened around my neck, cutting off my breath. I couldn't speak. I could only watch as his cruel face leaned closer to mine. >> you fooling? Today, you're going to know the price of crossing me. >> Mancio tossed me aside, then motioned to his men. They surrounded Pardo and kicked him mercilessly. Blood poured onto the ground in bright, shocking splashes. My hands shook uncontrollably, and I tried to push myself up, desperate to stop them. In my panic, my hand brushed against something. It was a gun. I raised the gun and aimed it at the men. "Let go of my brother!" Seeing the gun, they slowly backed off. Once they scattered, I rushed forward to pick Pardo up. "Pardo, are you okay? I'm getting you out of here." >> [groaning] >> Thanks to the training I had, I managed to hoist Pardo onto my back. Despite the pain radiating through my body, I rushed down the mountain. I just needed to get to the bottom of the mountain. We'd be safe. But just when I was a step away from the bottom, I felt a tug from behind me. Someone grabbed Pardo and dragged him back to the ground. His wounds were aggravated, and he coughed up blood. Barely able to breathe, I turned to see Mancio's cruel smile. >> You really think you can leave? >> His men closed in around us and started laughing. A massive scarred man stepped forward. Although I had trained in boxing, facing this giant was beyond my ability. >> me. Go. >> Pardo's weak voice reached me. I grabbed his arm, holding on to him tightly. >> No, I won't leave alone. We'll leave together. >> Mancio slowly clapped. >> Such touching sibling affection. >> His eyes glinted with malice as he mocked us. >> Let me make the decision for you. Neither of you is leaving. >> He waved his hand and the scarred man kicked us to the ground. The surrounding men closed in. I heard iron rods scraping against the ground and saw someone pull out a gun. I threw myself on top of Pardo, shielding him. Pardo couldn't get hurt. Not now, not ever. I repeated those words in my mind, bracing for the pain. Then a loud bang rang out and the iron rod of the person at the front fell to the ground. It was the Vicinos. They had arrived. >> Who dares to lay a hand on the Vicino family's young Don and Principessa? >> With a few gunshots, they took down all of Mancio's men. I urgently grabbed the butler to take Pardo to the hospital. >> Pardo isn't going to make IT IF WE DON'T HURRY! >> PARDO HAD ALREADY been severely injured in the car accident, yet he still protected me. If he didn't get treatment soon, his life would be at risk. I couldn't let my thoughts go any further. Unease clouded my mind. After the butler finally got Pardo into the operating room, I felt my racing heart slow down. Suddenly, everything went black and I lost consciousness. When I woke up, a full day had passed. I opened my eyes and found Imelda sitting beside my hospital bed holding my hand. "Livia, you're finally awake. Do you feel pain anywhere?" "What about Pardo? How is he?" At the mention of Pardo, Imelda's eyes darkened with a glint of anger. >> "He's in the ICU. The doctor said as long as he wakes up, he'll be fine. This isn't the end. Your papa and I will make sure the Sesa family pays for what they've done." >> Before I could respond, a doctor entered the room with the news that Pardo had regained consciousness. Imelda and I rushed out of the ward. >> "Don't worry. Mr. Vicino's leg injuries were severe, but he was brought in on time. His legs have been saved. If it had been any later, the outcome could have been much worse. Now, all he needs is rest." >> Upon hearing that, I finally let out a sigh of relief. I finally changed Pardo's fate of being crippled in his past life. Three days later, Pardo was moved to a regular ward. Alano scolded him for his recklessness, but Pardo didn't seem to care. His eyes were fixed on me. >> "Livia, how are you? Are you all right?" >> This was the kindest tone I had ever heard him speak to me since I joined the Vicino family. It wasn't just me. Alano and Imelda were equally taken aback. With one hand, Imelda pulled me to the bedside and she stroked Pardo's face with the other. >> "You can't be so reckless anymore. Once you're discharged, you need to study hard with Livia and catch up on the training you missed. After you graduate high school, you'll be ready for family duties." >> Every time they mentioned waiting until high school graduation to join the family business, Pardo would usually protest. But this time, he nodded obediently. He turned his gaze back to me. >> All right. I'll do it with Livia. >> Imelda's grip tightened on my shoulder. At that moment, I truly felt like I had a family. Alano made sure to deal with the Sessa family once and for all. He joined forces with other mafia families to take control of all Sessa family resources, avenging both Pardo and me. Pardo spent a month in the hospital, and I took a leave of absence from school to stay with him. During that time, I helped him catch up on high school courses and boxing theory. When Pardo was discharged and returned to school, it happened to coincide with the upcoming exams. After the exams, we walked out of the school gate, only to run into two people I hated, Dario and Regina. Seeing us, Regina feigned surprise and asked, "You're actually here for the exam? I heard you were badly injured. Are you okay?" I ignored her and pulled Pardo to walk past them. >> Livia! >> Dario called out to me. He didn't wear his usual disdainful expression. Instead, he looked somewhat guilty. >> Are you okay? >> I remembered the day he had turned away coldly. Even a stranger wouldn't have just walked off like that. My feelings for him from my previous life finally withered away. >> I'm fine. >> I replied flatly. Just as we were about to walk away, Dario stopped me again. But Pardo couldn't take it anymore and kicked him to the ground. >> [screaming] >> Don't you dare lay a hand on my sister. Unless you have a death wish. >> Dario clutched his stomach, clearly wanting to say something, but Regina stepped up to hold him back. >> Dario, let's go. Just ignore them. >> As he hesitated, Regina dragged him away. Pardo spat in their direction. >> Who do they think they are to talk to my sister? >> I couldn't help but laugh as I pulled him along. >> Enough, Pardo. Let's go home. >> Okay. I'm telling you this exam was a breeze for me. And my boxing skills have definitely improved a lot. >> I nodded seriously. I believe you. His learning ability had always been impressive. Even when he used to slack off, he kept his brain at a decent level. I noticed a clear improvement in his studies this month. As it turned out, my instincts were right. When the exam results were announced, Pardo soared into the top 10 at school. And I was the number one. All those students who had been waiting to see our grades were completely shocked. Regina gripped her frustration. >> THIS IS IMPOSSIBLE! YOU TWO MUST HAVE CHEATED! >> REGINA WENT WILD, storming into the principal's office to demand an investigation. Even Dario couldn't stop her. She smugly warned me. >> Even if you're from the Vicino family, if they find out you cheated, you'll both be expelled. Dario grabbed her, his anger flaring as he demanded that she apologize to me. Regina snapped, "Dario, you're my brother. Why are you siding with her?" "Do you have feelings for her?" Dario didn't say anything. Regina, in a fit of rage, SCREAMED AT HIM. FINE! I WON'T LET THEM GET AWAY WITH THIS! SOON AFTER, Pardo and I were summoned to the principal's office. After the school conducted its investigation, it was clear that neither Pardo nor I had cheated. On the contrary, Regina was expelled for spreading rumors and causing a scene at school. Why? It's them. IT'S THEIR FAULT. WHY SHOULD I BE EXPELLED? Regina went wild, attempting to assault the school administrators, accusing the teacher of taking bribes from the Vicino family and targeting Dario. She demanded that the school expel the teacher. In the heat of the argument, she accidentally injured the teacher, landing herself in a juvenile detention center. As her brother, Dario became an outcast, subjected to bullying. Dario was so worn out from the bullying that his grade plummeted, leading to a string of warnings from his homeroom teacher. If he couldn't get his scores back up, he'd be expelled. [music] Amid the gossip, Pardo and I were in the middle of a heated debate over a math problem. I felt a burning gaze and looked up to find Dario watching us. He looked frail and haggard now. I was so focused on convincing Pardo about the problem that I didn't spare Dario another glance. As graduation day approached, both Pardo and I began taking over family affairs. We were immersing ourselves in learning to manage the family business, leaving us no time to worry about anyone else. On graduation day, everyone was celebrating. Pardo rushed home to prepare for the graduation party. As I stood by the school gate, I saw a familiar figure waiting for me. Dario? He had lost so much weight. His cheeks were sunken and his overall appearance was pitiful. He slowly walked toward me and asked, >> Which college are you going to? >> I was taken aback. What does it matter to you? I distinctly remembered how he had always despised me in this life, even going as far as forbidding Regina from approaching me. After a moment of silence, he hesitated before speaking again. >> I've been having this recurring dream lately. In it, you're my sister and we even get married. We were so happy. >> He looked at me with such hopeful eyes that I was briefly dazed. He must have remembered his last life, too, but unfortunately, I gave him a faint smile. You said it yourself. It's just a dream. Ignoring his shattered expression, I walked toward the car waiting for me. And so, I finally severed ties with my last life and stepped into a brand new future that was all mine.

transcript.fullText: On my 20th birthday, I had to choose a husband before all of Olympus. Everyone thought I would choose Apollo's Olympian, the radiant heir of the sun god, and the man I had loved for years. In my last life, I did. Because of me, he gained Zeus's favor, sacred estates, and the right to rise above every divine heir. But after our marriage, he gave his sunlight to Syltest, the dying flower nymph my mother had taken in. >> Your light was meant to belong to Persephone. >> And who else would be worthy if not you? >> When Demeter drove her away, Apollo blamed me. >> It was you. I loved you for 10 years. >> That was your choice. No one ever asked you to love me. Persephone, my daughter, who will you choose to be your husband? >> Faced with Zeus' question, I spoke the name without hesitation. Cassian. The last bloodline of Hades, the cursed prince of the underworld whom everyone mocked. The sons of the old houses went quiet when they saw me. >> Look who came back to beg again. Persephone really cannot stay away from Apollo's sunshine. A daughter of Zeus chasing a man like a lovesick mortal. Olympus must be proud. >> [laughter] >> If the old king knew she was using his oath to force a marriage, even the thunder would be ashamed. >> They didn't bother lowering their voices. In my last life, every word would have cut me. Now, I looked at Apollo and felt nothing but a clean, cold distance. He looked me over with familiar contempt. >> What are you doing in my grandfather's wing? Asking Lord Zeus to plead for you? Or reminding him that your mother's blood once saved Olympus during the Titan raids? >> Zeus summoned me. Tomorrow is my 20th birthday. He will host the choosing himself. Everyone knew Zeus' oath. The man I chose would receive my dowry, access to the thunder vaults, and the right to stand beside me in the new council. In my last life, I had chosen Apollo and placed a crown in his hands. He stepped closer, already smiling like a victor. >> After marriage, we will live by sensible rules. I will not be tied to one woman, and you will not interfere with the healings I perform for Celeste. If you can accept that, I may treat you kindly. >> I almost laughed. He spoke as if I were still waiting for scraps. Before I could answer, a soft cough came from the far archway. Celeste crossed the hall in a pale green gown, her hair braided with white blossoms. Her cheeks looked fragile, her eyes damp, and her hand rested over her heart as if every breath cost her pain. >> Persephone, Demeter asked me to come with you. She worried you would feel lonely among Apollo's people. >> Anxiety written all over his face. He kissed Celesta and poured his sunlight into her. >> Why did you leave the garden when you are weak? >> I only wanted to help. He turned on me. >> You cannot even attend a meeting without dragging her into your drama. She is ill. Must everything serve your pride? >> In my last life, I would have explained that I had not asked Celeste to come. I would have cried, argued, and looked like the jealous woman they wanted me to be. This time, I only smiled. You two look busy. I will not interrupt. Apollo's face darkened. >> Do not play cold with me, Persephone. If you keep acting like this, I may refuse you tomorrow. >> Good. I deliberately glanced down at the obvious reaction beneath his clothes. That sounds like excellent news to me. I walked away before he understood. The birthday feast began at sunset. Every old house sent gifts heavy enough to make their loyalty clear. Apollo arrived late with Celeste on his arm. A faint gold mark shone at the base of her throat. In my last life, I would have felt the room tilt. Now, I merely looked away and continued speaking to Athena's priestess beside me. Apollo noticed. He moved Celesta behind him, ready for tears, accusations, anything he could turn against me. When I gave him nothing, his mouth tightened. >> You are pretending to be generous because you are afraid I will not marry you. >> I lifted my cup. Think whatever comforts you. >> I am the heir of the sun. A man in my position will never belong to one woman. If you behave, I may still give you the respect of a wife. >> He drew a small gold box from his robe. Inside lay a bracelet of dawn stone. Apollo, it is beautiful. Is this from Helios's private forge? She looked at me quickly. But, but it is Persephone's birthday gift. I should not take what belongs to her. Apollo closed the box and placed it in her palm. >> Keep it if you like it. I can buy Persephone another. She likes anything from me. >> A memory rose before I could stop it. Years ago, Apollo had given me a cloak in the rain because I was soaked through. I kept it for months. When he found it folded in my room, he told half the court I was shameless enough to treasure a servant's kindness as love. I am leaving. Apollo caught my wrist. >> Upset already? You will share my bed sooner or later. Why act pure now? >> Do not touch me. >> [laughter] >> Still pretending? Who else would you choose? Cassius Hadeon? The last scrap of Hades, hidden in the shadow wing because even Olympus cannot decide whether to pity him or fear him? He cannot stand in the sun without looking half dead. His underworld wings were shattered in the chariot fall that killed his parents. Some say he will never fly again. Some say the darkness broke more than that. Is that the husband you want, Persephone? >> At the hall entrance, a shadow moved. Cassian Hadeon stood beneath the bronze arch, dressed in black with a silver clasp at his throat. He no longer used the wheelchair I remembered from the old rumors. But his cloak fell heavily over his back, hiding the ruined line of his wings. His face was pale, his dark eyes calm. >> You may insult me if it pleases you, Apollo. But you will speak to Lady Persephone with respect. >> Unlike Apollo, he didn't look around to see who admired him. He bowed to Zeus first, then to the altar flame. And when his gaze reached me, it held no mockery, no pity, and no demand. That steadiness hurt more than any insult. In my last life, I had wasted years begging Apollo to look at me with even half that respect. I wanted to say his name then and there. >> If you choose the Hecaton boy, keep silent until I announce it. The vaults have too many hungry eyes. >> So, I swallowed the words. Cassian looked at me once. Something like disappointment crossed his face and disappeared toward the shadowed side of the hall. >> I will never trouble you. >> Celeste smiled beside Apollo as if she had won. The guests pointed at the golden ribbons tied to the banners, symbols of Apollo's victory. >> Look at that. Apollo is certain to win Persephone's hand with ease. After all, Persephone has been hopelessly devoted to Apollo for years. >> I entered with Demeter's gifts and found Celeste waiting by the fountain. She wore pearls, dawn stones, and a golden girdle I recognized from Apollo's private treasury. Do you like them? Apollo said, "Fragile flowers deserve gentle things." I told him it was too much, but he insisted. I stepped around her. She moved into my path. Do not look so cold, Persephone. I know you are jealous, but love cannot be forced. Apollo chose where his heart wanted to rest. Before I TOUCHED HER, >> [screaming] >> SHE folded to the floor with a cry. Persephone, why would you push me? >> [gasps and laughter] >> I know you hate me, but Demeter raised me, too. Apollo arrived as if the scene had been rehearsed for him, then looked up with fury bright in his face. >> Have you no shame, bullying a dying nymph at Zeus's festival? >> She fell on purpose. transcript.fullText: Are you sure you want to transfer the two billion dollars in shares? >> The doctor told me I had 72 hours left unless I got access to the newest experimental treatment. >> Her kidney failure is more critical. >> I nodded and swallowed the white pills that would only speed up my death. In the time I had left, I got a lot done. >> Are you sure you want to transfer the two billion dollars in shares? >> The lawyer's hand trembled as he passed me the documents. Yes. Give them to Yvonne. >> My daughter, Candace Lither, was giggling in Yvonne's arms. >> Mommy, Yvonne bought me a new dress. >> It looks beautiful. Make sure you always listen to Mommy Yvonne, okay? The art gallery I built from the ground up now had Yvonne's name on the sign. >> You're too kind, Kathleen. >> You'll run it even better than I ever did. I even signed all my parents' trust fund away. That was when Bowen finally gave me his first genuine smile in years. >> Kathleen, you've changed. You're not so aggressive anymore. You're beautiful like this. >> This dying version of me finally became the perfect Kathleen Sullivan in their eyes. Obedient, generous, and no longer argumentative. The 72-hour countdown had already begun, and I couldn't help but wonder what they would remember when my heart stopped for good. The good wife who finally learned to let go, or the woman who completed her revenge by dying? But Yvonne needs it more, right? My husband, Bowen Lindell, said I was not gentle enough. My parents called me selfish, and my daughter said she loved Yvonne Lawson more. So, I decided to spend my last 72 hours giving everything I had, my life, my legacy, to this perfect woman. >> It's late-stage cancer. If you don't start the special treatment immediately, you have at most 3 days. >> I leaned back in the hospital bed and stared out the window. I had poured myself into this marriage for 7 years as Bowen's wife until she appeared. >> You okay? >> I'm fine. >> The doctor said you need that experimental treatment, but >> But Yvonne needs it more, right? Yvonne was the pitiful girl I convinced my parents to adopt from the orphanage when I was 12. I treated her like a real sister, never imagining she would take everything from me one day. >> You have to understand. Eve's condition is worse. Her kidneys are close to failing and you you still look fine. >> Yeah, I looked okay. No one knew I had been secretly taking fatal doses of painkillers just to numb the agony that the cancer was causing. I understand. Let her have the treatment. Relief washed over Bowen's face. >> I knew you'd understand. You've changed a lot these past few years. You're not so stubborn anymore. >> Stubborn? I laughed bitterly to myself. Ever since Yvonne came into our lives, every time I stood my ground, it was labeled as jealousy and pity. >> What? Kathleen, that's your beloved gallery. >> That evening, I forced myself to go home. >> Mommy. >> My daughter, Candace Linser, saw me and immediately hid behind Yvonne. >> Hey Candace. >> I managed to smile. >> Kathleen, you're back. >> Yvonne said, wearing the luxury suit I had given her. She was sitting in what used to be my spot. Yv, I have something for you. I walked to the study and returned with a folder. These are the transfer papers for my art gallery. I want to give it to you. >> What? Kathleen, that's your beloved gallery. >> Yes, it was the gallery I had built from the ground up, my life's work. However, at that point, none of that mattered anymore. I smiled. You're better suited to run it than I am. Consider it an early wedding gift. Yvonne's expression flickered, but she quickly resumed her innocent look. >> Kathleen, what are you talking about? I stepped closer and whispered, "I know everything. It's okay. I wish you both well." Bowen walked in just then, looking tense when he saw us together. >> What are you two talking about? >> Kathleen wants to give me the gallery. Yvonne said with tears in her eyes. She's being so kind. Bowen looked at me, complex emotions flashing in his eyes. >> Kathleen Sullivan, you >> I'm tired. I said, interrupting him. "I'm going upstairs to rest. Candace, be good and listen to Aunt Yvonne." "Okay." Candace replied flatly. Then she turned to Yvonne. >> Mommy Yvonne, let's keep playing our game. >> My heart clenched when I heard her addressing her as Mommy Yvonne. I knew they would regret it all, but I would already be gone by then. Back in the bedroom, I leaned against the door and finally collapsed. The cancer cells were devouring my life, and those drugs were accelerating the process. Later, I began sorting through my closet. Those expensive dresses, jewelry, and handbags would all belong to Yvonne soon. >> You have 72 hours left. >> Kathleen, for these last 3 days let them remember a perfect version of you. I knew the truth would come out eventually. Everything after my death had already been arranged, and the evidence I collected would expose who Yvonne really was. I knew they would regret it all, but I would already be gone by then. That would be my revenge. The next morning, I woke up in excruciating pain. The cancer cells burned through my body like flames, but the painkillers helped me maintain a calm facade. I forced myself out of bed. There was so much left to do. Walking down the stairs, I heard Candace's laughter coming from the living room. She was sitting on Yvonne's lap, reading a picture book together. >> Mommy Yvonne, this princess is so pretty. >> She is, just like you, Candace. Yvonne replied gently, kissing her forehead. When Candace saw me, she only glanced up briefly before returning to her book as if I were just an insignificant stranger. Good morning, Candace. >> Morning. >> She replied dismissively. Then tugged on Yvonne's hand. >> Mommy Yvonne, can we go to the garden and look for butterflies? >> Just a second, sweetheart, Yvette said, pretending to look concerned as she glanced at me. Your mommy might want to talk to you. It was not just the physical pain anymore, but my heart was breaking, too. >> I don't want to hear it. Mommy's always busy and never plays with me. >> Candace pouted. Her words sliced through me like a knife. She was right. I had spent less time with her over the years because of work, while Yvette always had time for Candace. It's okay. Go ahead and have fun. I replied with a strained smile. As I watched them walk off hand in hand, I had to grip the wall just to stay upright. It was not just the physical pain anymore, but my heart was breaking, too. In the dining room, Bowen was watching the financial news. When he saw me come in, he only looked up briefly. He frowned and said, >> You look awful. Stop pushing yourself so hard. >> I'm fine. Anyway, I want to talk to you about something. >> What is it? >> He put down his iPad impatiently. I pulled out the documents I had prepared. It's about our pre-nup. I want to make some changes. Bowen took the papers and looked at them. >> Kathleen, you want to give up all your property rights? >> I replied calmly, yes. If something happens to me, if there's an accident, I want all the assets to go to you, including the trust fund my parents left me. >> What? >> I also want to give my art collection to Eve. >> Even your mother's original Monet? >> She loves art and will better manage it than I can. Consider it an early wedding gift. The air instantly grew thick with tension, and Bowen looked at me coldly. >> Kathleen, what exactly are you trying to pull? >> I remained calm. I'm not trying to pull anything. I'm just tired and ready to let go. >> THAT'S TWO BILLION DOLLARS WORTH OF SHARES! >> HIS EXPRESSION CHANGED, and he muttered, >> You know, don't you? >> The hotel surveillance, credit card bills, and Candace calling her mommy Yvette. I smiled bitterly. Bowen, do you really think I don't know anything? >> [snorts] >> I don't blame you. It's my fault. I was always arguing with you about company matters, always so controlling. Yvette is gentle and considerate, and she never contradicts you. She's better suited for you. >> Kathleen! >> I stood up. This afternoon, I'll go to the office to announce that I'm transferring my shares to Yvette. I'll make her an official member of the board. >> YOU'VE LOST YOUR MIND! >> Bowen shot up from his chair. >> THAT'S TWO BILLION DOLLARS WORTH OF SHARES! >> I HAVEN'T LOST MY MIND. I said, looking out at Yvette and Candace in the garden. I just want all of you to be happy. From today onward, Yvette will represent me in all company decisions. She said, "The gallery made 200 million this year. You'd be proud. I remember you once wrote in your journal that you dreamed of making it the best in New Eraval. Well, it is now. Dad's still the same. After everything, he never dated again. He said hurting you once was already unforgivable, and he didn't want to make the same mistake twice. Grandma and Grandpa passed away last year. Before they left, they told me to tell you that they loved you. They always did. They just realized it too late." >> Candace's voice dropped to a whisper. And Javon? She lost her mind in prison. The doctor said it was a full mental breakdown. Maybe that's karma. >> However, life had no what-ifs. The cemetery was quiet, with only the sound of wind and distant birdsong. Mom, you know what I regret the most? It's those words, I hate you. I've spent 20 years trying to take them back. Every time I remember the way you looked at me that day, I wish I could turn back time. Annie told me you tried to send me a message before you died. I wonder what it was. Was it an I love you? Or maybe a take care of yourself? I'll never know. She pulled a picture frame from her bag, a yellowed photo from when she was born with Kathleen holding her. Kathleen looked so happy in the photo, her eyes full of maternal love. This is the most precious thing I own. Candace placed the frame gently in front of the grave. Every time I look at it, I wonder what if. What if she had not been blinded by Ivan? What if she had seen who truly loved her? What if she had told her mom just once, I love you? However, life had no what ifs. Every night he dreamed that Kathleen was still alive. Bowen's car was parked not far away. He had aged considerably, his temples already gray. The once ambitious business elite looked like just an ordinary middle-aged man. She's been there for a while. Annie said from the passenger seat. Over the years, she had stayed by their side caring for both father and daughter. Let her stay a little longer. Bowen replied as he watched his daughter's silhouette. >> This is her time with Kathleen. Let her stay a little longer. >> Bowen replied as he watched his daughter's silhouette. >> This is This is her time with Kathleen. >> Aren't you going over? >> No. >> He said with a bitter smile. >> [snorts] >> I don't deserve to stand in front of her. God! >> Even after 20 years, he could not forgive himself. Every night he dreamed that Kathleen was still alive and nothing had happened. Then, he would wake up every morning to the cruel reality. >> Tracy laid her bouquet down. As evening approached, a young woman came to the grave. Hello. Can I help you? >> Candace he looked at her with confusion. The woman's eyes were brimming with tears. >> I'm Tracy Summers, a pancreatic cancer patient. 5 years ago, the Kathleen Sullivan Cancer Foundation saved my life. I came here today to thank her. >> I'm sure she can hear you. Tracy laid her bouquet down and bowed deeply. >> Mrs. Sullivan, thank you. Because of you, I'm alive today and can watch my children grow up. >> Candace had witnessed scenes like this countless times. Every person the foundation had helped remembered Kathleen's name. What her mother had exchanged her life for was not only her family's regret, but also new life and hope for thousands of strangers. As night fell, Candace finally rose to her feet, ready to leave. She glanced at the headstone one last time and whispered softly, >> "Mom, you once asked if we would remember you. The answer is every single day and every moment for the rest of our lives." >> And the love On her way home, Candace opened the journal Kathleen had left behind. She had received it on her 18th birthday. It recorded every precious detail from the day Kathleen found out she was pregnant to Candace's fifth birthday. The last entry was written one week before Kathleen's death. Kathleen's journal, "My sweet Candace, you called Yvonne Mommy Yvonne again today. It broke my heart, but I don't blame you. You're still too young to tell truth from lies. I only hope that one day, when you grow up and understand, you won't hate yourself too much. I've never blamed you, and I never will, because loving you has been the happiest thing in Mommy's life." >> On the very last page, there was a line of hurried handwriting. "If there's a next life, I still want to be your mom." Candace hugged the journal tightly to her chest and wept uncontrollably outside the window. New Eraval remained bustling with lights and life. However, there would always be a void in that city, a missing piece named Kathleen Sullivan, a woman who defined motherhood with her own life, a woman who finally became the perfect well-behaved daughter they all once wanted, a woman who would forever live in their hearts. That was the end. That was the end of the story, but the grief and the love would never truly end.

As the daughter of the king of the entire realm, I had to choose one of the lords from the two major realm tribes as my political spouse. When I opened my eyes again, I returned to the time before marrying him. This life, I decided to fulfill his love affair. But unexpectedly, Cain would go crazy with regret for me. Just as I walked out of the council hall and crossed the training ground, I saw him, Cain. He was training with the soldiers, accompanied by that giant ice plain white wolf. Without even raising his head, he commanded sternly, >> Pick it up. >> Yes! >> The soldiers instantly froze, their eyes fixed on me, waiting to see a good show. I knew this trick too well. Well, Eve, you've changed your tune. Only days ago you were utterly devoted to him, and now you put on princely airs as a princess. You were once his shadow, clinging to his side every day.
